matches.context: Slovakia have already won Group C3 on 11 points, so this game decides second place. Moldova are second on 7 points (goals 5-9) and the Faroe Islands third on 5 (7-7) after drawing all five games; a Faroes win lifts them to 8 and above Moldova, while a draw or a Moldova win keeps Moldova second. Kazakhstan, on 2 points, host Slovakia today. The reverse fixture in Chișinău on 29 September ended 1-1: Viljormur Davidsen scored a penalty for the Faroes, and Moldova had 20 attempts to 6 and 63% possession (UEFA match report). On 13 November the Faroes drew 2-2 in Košice and Moldova beat Kazakhstan 2-1 at home, their second 2-1 win over Kazakhstan after the one in Astana on 2 October. Both teams have scored in all five Faroes games, and neither side has kept a clean sheet in the campaign (statz.ai).

Bulgaria have 4 (3-10) and Luxembourg 3 (2-8), and Estonia host Bulgaria in the other game. The group winners go up to League B, so a win guarantees Iceland first place. A draw would almost certainly be enough too: Iceland and Estonia drew both their meetings (1-1, 0-0), and on UEFA's usual tie-breakers Iceland's goal difference (+11) is nine better than Estonia's (+2). Iceland won the reverse fixture 3-0 in Luxembourg on 29 September. On 13 November Iceland won 5-0 in Bulgaria and Luxembourg lost 1-0 at home to Estonia, their fourth defeat in a row without scoring. Iceland have kept clean sheets in four of their five group games. The game is in Reykjavík: the groundskeeper says the undersoil-heated pitch is free of frost, with -3°C forecast for Monday.

matches.context: The Netherlands top Group A2 with 11 points (14-5) and are unbeaten. Germany (6-3) and Greece (5-10) have 8 each, and Serbia have none. Greece host Serbia at the same time. Greece lead Germany on head-to-head (1-0 in Germany, 0-0 in Athens), so Germany must win to be sure of a top-two place. A draw is only enough if Serbia beat Greece. The Netherlands are practically through: Sports Mole says only a 14-goal swing in goal difference would knock them out, and a draw or better keeps them top (RotoWire). The reverse fixture in Amsterdam on 24 September ended 1-1: Felix Nmecha scored first and Cody Gakpo equalised in stoppage time. Matchday 5 on 13 November: Serbia 1-3 Germany (Babić own goal, Wirtz, Gruda; Serbia finished with nine men) and Netherlands 7-0 Greece (Reijnders first-half hat-trick, Timber 2, Summerville, Malen).

matches.context: Group 2 is decided on Monday, and only the top two reach the quarter-finals. The Netherlands lead on 11 points (14-5) after beating Greece 7-0 in Amsterdam on 13 November. Greece (5-10) and Germany (6-3) both have 8, and Serbia (4-11) are certain to finish bottom after a fifth straight defeat, 1-3 at home to Germany. Greece beat Germany 1-0 away and drew 0-0 at home, so they lead the head-to-head. By our reading of UEFA's tie-breakers, Greece go through if Germany lose to the Netherlands, need at least a draw if Germany draw, and are out whatever they do if Germany win: a Greece win would then create a three-way tie on 11 points, and the 7-0 puts Greece last in that mini-table. Greece won the reverse fixture 2-1 in Belgrade on 24 September with a stoppage-time winner from Anastasios Douvikas, and they are unbeaten at home in the group (2-2 v Netherlands, 0-0 v Germany).

news.text: Bojan Miovski was left out of the squad by coach Goce Sedloski for lack of minutes at Rangers. Gjoko Zajkov, Andrej Stojchevski and Tihomir Kostadinov are also not in the squad.

Darko Churlinov returned after missing four games over a visa issue and started at Hampden, in a front three with Doriev and Rastoder. Nikola Serafimov, Boban Nikolov, Imran Fetai and Stefan Despotovski were recalled for this window.

North Macedonia lost 2-1 in Glasgow on 13 Nov, their fifth defeat in five group games and their first goal of the campaign. Their winless run reached 10 games with the 2-0 loss in Ljubljana in September.
Benjamin Šeško (shin) misses another window and is not expected back until early 2027.
Timi Max Elšnik was injured playing for Crvena zvezda and is not in the squad. Cesar did not call up a replacement.
Erik Janža and David Zec served one-match bans against Switzerland after their second bookings of the campaign in Glasgow, so both should be available again.

Against Switzerland, Slovenia switched to a back four, with Zaletel and Kuzmić in and Karničnik in midfield. Sandi Lovrić, who scored in the reverse fixture, and Andraž Šporar were on the bench. Atalanta's Relja Obrić, 20, has his first senior call-up.

matches.context: Malta lead Group D1 with 7 points from three games (W2 D1, goals 4-2) and are already sure of first place: Andorra have finished on 4 points and Gibraltar can reach at most 5. Gibraltar have 2 points (D2 L1, goals 1-3). A win would lift them above Andorra into second, and a draw or a defeat leaves them third. The reverse fixture in Malta on 1 October ended 1-1, with Joseph Mbong scoring on 53 minutes and James Scanlon equalising on 61. On 13 November Gibraltar lost 2-0 in Andorra. Malta had no group game that week and drew 1-1 with Eswatini in a friendly on 12 November. Gibraltar have scored once in three group games and have not won.
